newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM Hun Sen says family in danger.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM Hun Sen says family in danger.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen on Thursday said police were investigating two suspects for allegedly plotting to assassinate members of the leader's family, his friends and staff.
Speaking at a market opening in this Mekong River town, Hun Sen did not elaborate on the investigation, but he warned anyone against threatening those close to him.
"I would like to warn, please do not do anything crazy," said Hun Sen.

On Sunday grenades ripped through a demonstration led by opposition Khmer Nation Party (KNP) leader Sam Rainsy, killing 19 people and wounding more than 100 in the worst urban political violence in years.

Sam Rainsy, who narrowly escaped injury, has accused Hun Sen of being behind the blasts. The co-premier has denied responsibility and condemned the violence but suggested that the protest leaders should be arrested.
In his speech, Hun Sen said he was not talking about an idle threat against those close to him, noting that his brother-in-law had been shot dead in November of last year.
He has said his family was threatened before.
Since Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP) formed a coalition government with the royalist FUNCINPEC party after U.N.-run elections in 1993, the arrangement has been marked by periods of tension.

Police aligned to the CPP have linked Sam Rainsy to the killing of Hun Sen's brother-in-law Keo Samuth and have charged the KNP security chief, Surn Vong Vannak, with involvement in the murder. Sam Rainsy denies all the allegations.

"From now on the authorities, armed forces and police must make an effort to keep political stability and strengthen social and political security in order to protect people's lives and end violence," Hun Sen said.

The New York-based Human Rights Watch Asia called on the international community to demand an impartial and public investigation into the attack and to link future aid to effective moves to end violence and ensure justice.
